plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Silvery-green mounds erupt into slender spikes of fragrant violet-blue blossoms. Fields hum with bees and the air turns sweetly herbal. In Provence the rolling rows look like purple ripples across the countryside.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late June to August in the Northern Hemisphere, usually peaking in early to mid July
plants.location: Provence, France, and other Mediterranean-climate regions of Europe
plants.funFact: Lavender belongs to the mint family. Its name likely comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash', because the Romans scented their baths with it.

plants.name: Hydrangea macrophylla
plants.description: Big, rounded clusters of flowers weigh down the stems like pom-poms. They glow in shades that shift from sky blue to rosy pink. They are a classic feature of summer gardens and of coastal hedgerows.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early summer through late summer, with blooms commonly in full display in early July
plants.location: Gardens in the eastern United States, the British Isles and Japan
plants.funFact: Soil chemistry sets the color. Acidic soil with available aluminum yields blue blooms, while neutral to alkaline soil yields pink ones.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: The largest bloom of the protea family looks like a crown of silky, pointed bracts around a fuzzy center. In the cool, damp South African winter these dramatic flowers brighten the fynbos hillsides.
plants.bloomingSeason: Peak flowering is from late autumn to spring in the Southern Hemisphere, with some blooms from winter into early spring, so July is a time of flowering
plants.funFact: King Protea is South Africa's national flower. It has survived for millions of years in a fire-prone landscape, and its thick underground stems help it resprout after wildfires.
